name: spend-breakdown
title: Spend breakdown
description: Where every 100 goes: a ten-by-ten unit chart in tones and patterns, beside a legend that says what each share pays for.
docs: Pass title, description, parts (up to six, largest first, each with an id, a label, a share and a sentence on what it pays for) and optionally total (the whole as an amount, with a currency and a few words such as raised in 2025) and source (who says so, a link and a year). The shares are read as percentages of a hundred, and if they do not add up to 100 they are scaled, so the grid is always full. The hundred squares are allotted by the largest remainder method: 33.4, 33.3 and 33.3 become 34, 33 and 33 squares, the grid is exactly full, and the legend keeps the exact figures. Every part has a tone and a pattern of its own (solid, hatch, dots, cross hatch, a mid tone with sparse lines, vertical lines), so the chart still reads in greyscale and in print and no part looks like an empty square. The squares are hidden from assistive technology; the table beside them, with each percentage, name and sentence, is the content. Hovering a row of the legend keeps its squares lit and dims the rest, with no script. The percentage of a row is its row header, so a screen reader names a sentence by its share and not by the whole sentence. The legend sits beside the squares from 768px of width and under them on a narrower section, and on a small phone it gives up some padding so the sentences keep their room. Amounts are written short (€3.44M, €462K) with their digits pinned, so the server and the browser print the same text; where a locale's own data differs between the two runtimes (en-GB writes €4.2M in one and €4.2m in another) the figures are marked so the server's text stays and the page is not rebuilt. labels translates the fixed words, and the section renders on the server.
